transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t stop worrying. It feels like it’s all at once—my marriage, work, bills, things around the house I keep not finishing. And I keep thinking I’m failing as a husband and as a father.
How long have you been feeling this way, and does the worry seem to be about specific things in your life or more general and ongoing?

It’s been about nine months, I think. It really started when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and around the same time the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing. Since then it’s just felt ongoing, not like one small problem I can get past.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like trouble sleeping, restlessness, or muscle tension, that seem to go along with this worry?

Yeah. I feel wound tight almost all day, like my shoulders are locked up and I’m bracing for something. I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping pieces at chess club, because sitting still just feels impossible sometimes.
Have you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with your family?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. I still want to do those things, it’s just hard to relax enough to enjoy them. I wouldn’t say I’m constantly down, but I do feel worn out by all of this.
Do you feel like your worry is something you can’t control, even when you try to stop thinking about these problems?

Yeah, it feels really hard to control. I’ll try to tell myself, just focus on the code in front of me, or just get through a workout and breathe, but my mind keeps grabbing onto the next thing. One worry turns into another, and before I know it I’m imagining a bad review at work leading to losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. It feels like I can’t stop the chain once it starts.
Do you find yourself being easily startled or feeling on edge, like you’re constantly watching for something bad to happen?

Yeah, pretty much. I feel like I’m wound tight most of the day, like my shoulders are locked up and I’m sort of bracing for something. I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or tapping things at chess club, because just sitting still feels really hard.
